title: Harder instructions, weaker adherence
statement: Writer models keep to constraints less reliably as instructions get harder, and whether giving a writer only the rules its task needs, not the whole rulebook, fixes that is untested.
example: Across 18 models, average accuracy fell from 80.82% on the easiest constraint level to 36.76% on the hardest.
detail: A published evaluation of 18 models from six families found average accuracy falling from 80.82% at the easiest constraint level to 36.76% at the hardest (Ye et al. 2026, https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.99/). A Grade 3 proposal for steering a writer with explicit rules cited it as the strongest counter-evidence it faced, and drew its own inference, labelled as one: compile a small active contract rather than prompt with the full rule base (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0128-externalized-pedagogy-policy-compiler-decision.qmd`). The comparison the proposal planned never ran, because its experiment was stopped with those stages unrun (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0168-eppc-bias-experiment-terminal-kill-and-salvage.qmd`). To settle it: the same tasks written from the whole rule base and from only the rules that apply, across model families, scored on the same held-out artifacts.
against: The same study found that targeted training improved adherence, a remedy other than trimming the rules, and the proposal marks its own success estimate as personal confidence, not a research result (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0128-externalized-pedagogy-policy-compiler-decision.qmd`).

evidence.quote: across 18 models, constraint adherence fell materially as instruction difficulty increased, and targeted training improved it.
**Our architectural inference:** compile a small active contract rather than prompt with the full rule base
Formal artifact-renderer A was not run.
across 18 models, constraint adherence fell materially as instruction difficulty increased, and targeted training improved it.
Constraint interactions, ordering, and active-rule count create a measurable compliance ceiling.
